In the letter read above, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has stated that, the proposal was received from EMRI Green Health Services regarding the implementation of Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) to streamline the maintenance of the state's emergency ambulance fleet.

2. Tamil Nadu currently operates a fleet of 1,353 '108' ambulances, 130 JSSK vehicles, and 194 FHS project vehicles. However, the maintenance of this extensive fleet faces several critical hurdles:

The Original Equipment Manufacturer (Force Motors) has only 14 authorized service vendors across the state. Ambulances in districts without authorized vendors must travel long distances for minor repairs, leading to increased Nan-Case Kilometers (NCKM) and excessive fuel expenditure. Vehicles often remain off-road for more than a day for routine maintenance, significantly impacting emergency readiness.

3. The Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has further stated that:-

e The service provider proposes the pilot deployment of strategically located Mobile Service Vans and Mobile Service Bikes per region. These units will be equipped with essential diagnostic tools and spare parts to provide.

e On-site preventive maintenance at ambulance parking sites or

hospitals. . e Minor/medium repairs and immediate roadside breakdown assistance.

e In-house towing support to eliminate third-party charges. Cost Effectiveness and Financial Benefits:-

e The implementation is expected to be highly cost-effective, with projected savings arising from:

e Zero External Labour Costs: Utilizing in-house mobile technicians.

e Reduced Fuel Expenditure: Eliminating long-distance travel to workshops.

e Maximum Uptime: Aiming for near 100% fleet availability by reducing repair turnaround times.

4. Indicative pilot data for April 2026 suggests total monthly savings of approximately Rs.2,30,982/- across just three Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) units (TN20G1919, TN20G2298 and TN20G2144).

5. Considering the potential to optimize government assets and ensure uninterrupted emergency services to the public, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has requested the Government to consider and grant approval for this pilot initiative. The procurement, operation, and maintenance of the Mobile Service Vans will be entirely managed utilizing the regular, pre-approved operational budget of the 108 Ambulance Services.

Under the programme, children between 6 months and 59 months of age are provided prophylactic Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) syrup on a biweekly basis to prevent and control nutritional anaemia. The programme encompasses early screening and identification of anaemia, deworming, promotion of appropriate Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices, dietary diversification and improving awareness among caregivers regarding nutrition and hygiene. Regular growth monitoring, counselling and referral services for severely anaemic children are also undertaken through frontline health workers.

95

42.47 lakh under-five children received biweekly IFA syrup supplementation during the period of April 2025 – March 2026.

b). Junior WIFS

The programme addresses the management of anaemia among school-age children between 5 and 9 years by providing weekly Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation to improve haemoglobin levels and prevent iron deficiency anaemia. It emphasizes on nutrition education, promotion of iron-rich diets, hygiene, sanitation practices and regular health screening in schools improving the nutritional status, physical growth, cognitive development, learning capacity and overall health of children in this age group.

40.38 lakh children aged 5 to 9 years benefited from weekly IFA supplementation during the period April 2025 – March 2026.

3.9.5. Vitamin A Supplementation Programme

The Vitamin A Supplementation Programme is a targeted public health initiative aimed at providing paediatric dose Vitamin A syrup to infants and children aged 6 to 59 months, biannually ensuring wide coverage across all Districts. The

96

programme primarily aims to prevent childhood blindness by addressing Vitamin A deficiency, a leading cause of preventable visual impairment in children, while also significantly reducing child mortality from common infections such as measles, diarrhoea and boosting overall immune response to reduce the severity and frequency of illness in young children.

45,02,897 under five years of age received Vitamin A supplementation during the period April 2025 – March 2026.

3.9.6. National Deworming Day (NDD)

Albendazole tablets are administered biannually to children and adolescents aged 1–19 years through schools, Anganwadi Centres and healthcare institutions. Through large-scale preventive deworming and community awareness activities, the programme aims to reduce anaemia, malnutrition and worm-related morbidity while promoting better growth and overall well-being among children.
